chapters.title: Decide
chapters.headline: Decide what is worth building.
chapters.intro: Before any code: requirements a vendor can be judged against, options scored with evidence, and a clear call on whether to build, buy, or stop.

chapters.title: Ship
chapters.headline: Ship systems people rely on.
chapters.intro: From the IP-management platform an operations team runs its day on, to a Three.js showroom and AR try-on.

chapters.title: Learn
chapters.headline: Learn from what breaks.
chapters.intro: Every failure should make the next one harder. I write that down as tests, guards and tools, and some of those tools are open source.

decideStories.title: Four vendors, one decision
decideStories.body: For the trademark-monitoring platform I wrote the requirements, ran a four-vendor evaluation against them and made the build-vs-buy call. Then I led the in-house build with the team. It is in production.

decideStories.title: A finished build that missed the point
decideStories.body: After the business rejected a completed Power BI build, I re-scoped reporting as a custom module inside the platform instead of patching the wrong thing.

decideStories.title: A rollout gate for model output
decideStories.body: Model output that drives a legal recommendation is validated against historical outcomes before anyone relies on it. That is a condition of rollout, not a benchmark number.

decisionToy.title: Try it: when does the winner flip?
decisionToy.intro: A tiny version of decision-matrix. Move the weights and watch the ranking. A thin margin means your weights are deciding, not your options.
decisionToy.example: Example: replacing an ageing build server

mustHave.label: Must-have: data stays in our own region
mustHave.explain: A must-have is a yes/no gate, not a weight. Switch it on and an option that fails it cannot win, however well it scores.

decisionToy.fragileLabel: Fragile: a small change in weights flips this
decisionToy.footnote: Scores are illustrative. The full tool adds evidence per score, pairwise weighting and a decision record.

rtlLab.title: Arabic, done properly.
rtlLab.intro: Put a date or a phone number inside an Arabic sentence and the browser silently reorders it. The data is right; only the pixels are wrong, so users stop trusting the data. Flip the switch.

items.title: Look at the real data before writing the parser.
items.body: Formats you assume are formats you get wrong. More than once, a field I "knew" the shape of turned out to have two shapes, and the difference mattered.

items.title: Test in the real thing.
items.body: Scripted probes report success on broken paths. If it is a user interface, it is not done until it has been driven in a browser.

items.title: Make the failure mode expensive to reintroduce.
items.body: A bug that reached production comes back as a regression test, a database constraint or a type, so the same mistake fails loudly next time.

items.title: Say plainly what broke.
items.body: Status reports name what failed, why, and what changed. A clear bad-news report beats a vague good one.
